title: Horrible
content:
I’m extremely dissatisfied with my experience using Shopify and regret signing up.

Payout expectations were not made clear up front. I discovered after setup that even though my payout schedule was set to daily, that did not mean I would receive my funds the next business day. As a new account, each daily payout was effectively delayed by about 7 business days, which was completely different from what I expected and completely different from my previous payment processor, where I received funds the next business day from the start. The wording around daily payouts was misleading in practice because it suggested faster access to funds than what actually happened. That distinction between payout schedule and actual settlement timing was not made obvious during onboarding, and it should have been spelled out much more clearly before I committed to the platform.

The setup experience for the online store was also confusing and frustrating. Instead of one clear, cohesive onboarding flow, the process felt fragmented and difficult to follow. Basic setup did not feel intuitive, and it often seemed like important information was split across different areas rather than presented in one place. The platform did not feel user friendly, especially for someone trying to get a store operational efficiently.

The hardware setup was another major source of frustration. It took several days to figure out how to get everything working because the instructions for the overall system were not cohesive. Rather than having one clear end-to-end setup path, I had to piece together information from separate places, which made the process far more difficult and time-consuming than it should have been.

The overall experience has fallen far short of what was promised. Between the payout timing surprise, the lack of clear up-front communication, the confusing online store setup, and the difficult hardware setup, Shopify has been extremely disappointing and troublesome to use. At multiple points, it felt more like I was fighting the system than being supported by it.

Even the feedback process has been confusing. I was given a link to submit feedback, but it opened what appeared to be a chat and did not clearly indicate whether my feedback was actually being formally submitted. I couldn’t even get an email or form to send feedback so I had to resort to leaving a review. That added even more frustration to an already disappointing experience.

Avoid using this app before it’s too late. I’ve wasted tons of money and worse - time - on this terrible system.

title: Lots of room for improvement
content:
There are a lot of things that I like about the Shopify ap-
But there are more that I dislike about the whole program in general:
First off, with the amount of fraudulent orders that I receive, I lose money every transaction. The money is taken and then the order is canceled by a FLOW and then the money is returned but I lose money because of two reasons: a line of credit that’s in repayment, and the fee that Shopify takes even though I made zero profit from the refunded order. It’s absolute BS.
Second: it takes days to put money INTO the main balance account. So if you’re like me and don’t trust money to be left in anything but a central banking account, and this overdraft of fees happens after a fraudulent order, you get a million emails and notifications and threats while still waiting for funds to process that were initiated multiple days ago.
Third: it’s not an instant pay system like square, which means I operate on a separate system for markets, to instantly have the money in my account and not wait for a payout,  because the level of customization Shopify offers for branding is the best part about it.

content:

Shopify’s own Bill Pay feature that they offer for their Shopify Balance accounts did not pay my studio rent on time 2 months in a row despite being assured my rent payment would process. The first month they did offer a $50 reimbursement for the inconvenience. The second month this happened (which in my mind is worse because I had already spent hours upon hours dealing with them and their bill pay processing company Melio the first time to get it resolved) They refused to offer me a credit or even a written letter explaining their own  failure in paying bills with the money that was in my shopify balance account.

If you are a small business  just starting out save yourself the hassle and try Square. I have friends that swear by it. I am so disappointed with Shopify that I’m considering building a whole new Wordpress website just to get as far away from them as I can.

title: Shopify app update
content:
Hi Shopify team,

The recent update to the Shopify mobile app has made it much harder to manage inventory.

Previously, I could open a collection and quickly see the stock levels for every product within it. As a bakery owner, I use collections to plan production, and this view was one of the features I relied on most every week.

Now I have to open products individually or navigate through several extra screens, which adds a lot of unnecessary time to a task I perform daily.

Please consider bringing back the ability to view inventory quantities directly within collections on the mobile app, or add it as an optional list view. It was a simple but incredibly valuable feature for merchants managing stock.

Thank you for considering this feedback.

title: Issue going
content:
I’ve encountered several frustrating issues while using the Shopify app that have impacted my workflow:

Order Fulfillment Glitch: When fulfilling orders and scanning the tracking number, the app redirects me to the home page instead of confirming the tracking. I then have to go back to the orders page and manually confirm the order again, which is a repetitive and time-consuming process.
Website Customization Problems: While customizing my store, especially when sorting fields or blocks, the app freezes on the website and I have to refresh the page repeatedly. This issue happens consistently, which slows down my customization process and affects overall productivity.
Order Management Issue: When I try to open the orders section, the app now unexpectedly displays a message saying “Manage your orders – you will be notified when you get your first order.” The same message appears when accessing abandoned carts as well, which is confusing and prevents me from accessing important order and cart details.
These issues have made managing my store more difficult, and I hope they get addressed in future updates.

title: 1 month of silence from Shopify and $1,090 has disappeared from my payout account.
content:
I have so far had an absolutely terrible experience, and it is culminating in what seems to be $1,090 stolen from my payout account (and not in Balance either), with no help in sight.

Back in May I opened up a Shopify store selling Western-inspired golf apparel for women. This went on smoothly for the first month or so. Then, on June 29th I was made aware that my payouts were placed “on hold” and that my next steps were to check my email to find out how to resolve this. Now, the kicker is that my shop was featured in a small magazine article on the 28th of June, so I had about $1,000 in sales tied up in this “hold.” Upon checking my email, I realized I didn’t get one for whatever reason. I then messaged Shopify support, who assured me that this was being handled by the “payments team” and it was routine, and not to worry. This was all around July 1st. It has now been over a month (writing as of August 1st) and I have had no resolution. To boot, the $1,090 that was in my payout account is seemingly GONE. It is not in my Balance App (I have no external accounts linked) and not in my Shopify payout records. It has disappeared. I have messaged support about this 7-8 times over the course of the month and never get an answer. And I pay for a lower tier of Shopify, so I am not entitled to phone support. At this point I believe Shopify has taken my money. I have still NEVER received an email about this (in my spam folder or otherwise.) Terrible customer service and terrible resolution team.

I launched a book sale using Shopify yesterday. After 2k sales in 24 hours, I can say I’m overjoyed with the first day of sales. Unfortunately I have received dozens of messages, emails, dm’s from potential customers saying they are unable to access the website to purchase books. These of course, are only the customers who have taken the time to reach out.
This started at the beginning of sales yesterday and has continued today. My developer was on the phone with Shopify yesterday, I sent emails, and also was on the phone beginning again early this morning. After all of these calls we were given directives  to ask our customers to take their phones off of Wi-Fi to place orders, or try putting items in the cart and then choosing the payment method. Or use another device to access the site or change browsers when they were told the site was unsafe. We purchased a separate domain through Shopify as they suggested to funnel all of our transactions, and the website is being flagged as unsafe.
Shopify will not resolve the problem or put anyone on their technical team to immediately take care of this issue. I was told the tech team does not do phone calls, only emails. Also, they are backed up today.
I have stopped sharing about the book launch because we are experiencing so many customer problems regarding accessing the site and checking out.  Very disappointed that a brand with so many resources is unwilling to step up and resolve this for a small business owner.

title: Expensive to keep traffic coming
content:
Bad points I’ll start with.
If you want site visitors you need to have a good amount of money to get them to your store via social media and google ads. If you spend around £2000 that will get you around 30k shop visitors (obviously depending on what you’re selling) this may sound like a lot of store visitors but because your a ‘new’ website not many will actually buy. I’ve had a 0.05% conversion rate (which basically means I’ve spent more on ads and products on dropshipping than I have made in profit) If you stop the ads and have followers in social media you can expect your traffic to become zero) you need to spend money daily to keep the traffic coming.

You are kind of forced to add apps to help you sell, all these apps have massive up selling techniques by offering you a free trial, then start a monthly charge there after so watch out for these.

Good points.
Shopify response time to questions are unbelievably fast, they are willing to help at every stage and have a fantastic customer service (I’m really impressed)

Shopify is user friendly and even getting down to do abit of coding isn’t difficult with their walkthrough guides.

So to conclude shopify is great to use, very user friendly, customer service is great but if you’re drop shipping or you have a product to sell with no current social media followers you’ll have to dig deep in your pockets to keep the traffic coming. Maybe you might have a winning product and you’ll make a load of money or you’ll be like the majority and spend money on ads and reap no rewards short term (I’ve only been going 6 weeks so I can’t comment on long term, I will update this review once I’ve got another 5 months under my belt and another couple of grand spent on ads)

title: Be ready for the “Account on hold” malarkey
content: I’ve set up 3 Shopify stores now and I like the Shopify platform. However, there’s an issue to be aware of and it’s a bit sneaky. The moment you make a sale, Shopify will place your account on hold and ask you to verify your business with more information. I’ve no problem with this and I understand it’s a legal requirement - but, Shopify could easily have you complete the required information BEFORE you make your first sale (during setup). It’s obviously a sneaky ploy to make it easier for people to get started, but if you’re a bit of a procrastinator like me, you could easily find your money on hold while you argue with Shopify. Annoyingly, they have no awareness at all of U.K. law and things like the data protection act and will ask you for your suppliers’ or customers’ information regardless. Do the right thing Shopify and get all this done upfront before sellers get all busy.

title: PLEASE FIX THIS ONE THING
content:
When adding a product to my store, I am unable to select multiple photos to add to the product at a time.

To those people who regularly add new products and like to include many different photos to show all the different product options like colours and styles: be warned, you will spend more of your time in this app manually selecting and adding one photo at a time to one product at a time than anything else.

To those whose selection rarely changes: you’ll still spend more of your time adding photos in this tedious manor than anything else you do during your initial set up.
